title.narrative: Smrt.bio SAIL 2020: Validating ‘Scalable, Agile and Inspired Labour’ in South Africa

description.narrative: The labour market in South-Africa has a volume of almost 38 million people. The official unemployment-rate is almost 27% and the Expanded unemployment-rate is even 10% higher. Within the age-group of 15-24, the number of people that are Not in Education, Employment or Training (NEET), reaches a staggering 30% amongst historically disadvantaged individuals and out of the 250,000 students that graduate from Technical Vocational Schools (TIVET) each year, only 10,000 find a suitable job. Meanwhile, there are 500,000 permanent vacancies that cannot be filled. Sustainable job creation, youth employment and preparing for the industrial revolution 4.0 are top priorities in the country’s National Development Plan, as the labour market is becoming highly dynamic due to local challenges and technological developments for which the country needs to prepare. A paradigm shift is needed to cope with and prepare for these challenges and to improve cooperation on the labour market among its four key stakeholders: individuals, employers, education, and local public organisations, such as municipalities. Dutch company Smrt.bio developed a smartphone based talent mobilisation platform to enable and facilitate recruitment, HR management, talent development, and lifelong learning opportunities for candidates, micro SMEs and corporates. Using its own algorithms, gamification techniques, and 26,000 different competence based job description templates, the platform enables better and sustainable matches between candidates and employees, increases the candidates’ opportunities, reduces the barriers for individuals to apply for a job, stimulates continuous learning of potential candidates and reduces time and costs for employers to recruit new staff. The platform is available in both English, and Zulu.To prepare for further investments Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to validate the Smrt.Bio platform in the South African context. The project included public partner selection, piloting and adjusting the platform amongst 95 test-users, testing of different pricing and license models and developing a bankable business plan to attract further investments. The project supported 4 direct jobs, 3 indirect jobs and provided sustainable knowledge transfer by training nearly 100 people. Pending further investments, Smrt.Bio is looking to grow its presence in South Africa within the next 3 years, which may result in 81 new direct jobs and improved talent mobilisation, access to the labour market and skills development for at least 232 job seekers.
